steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# GRPO (verl FSDP + vLLM, rollout KV cache in fp8 for throughput) on an integer-answer math pool (Skywork-OR1 / POLARIS / DAPO-Math-17k)
3	# from Qwen/Qwen3-4B. Builds the RL parquet with scripts/make_rl_data.py, then trains.
4	# Env vars configure the run; extra Hydra overrides on the command line are appended last.
5	set -euo pipefail
6	WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
7	export WS
8	MODEL=${MODEL:-$WS/models/Qwen3-4B}
9	NGPU=${NGPU:-2}
10	EXP=${EXP:-grpo}
11	RESP=${RESP:-16384}
12	BS=${BS:-32}
13	MINI=${MINI:-16}
14	N=${N:-8}
15	LR=${LR:-1e-6}
16	STEPS=${STEPS:-3}
17	GPU_UTIL=${GPU_UTIL:-0.7}
18	KV_DTYPE=${KV_DTYPE:-fp8}
19	SEED=${SEED:-1}
20	MAXTOK=$(( RESP + 1024 ))
21	LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$WS/outputs/$EXP}
22	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
23	export PYTHONPATH="$WS/verl:$WS/third_party/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
24	export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline} WANDB_DIR="$LOG_DIR"
25	export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
26	
27	python3 "$WS/scripts/make_rl_data.py" > "$LOG_DIR/make_rl_data.log"
28	
29	python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
30	  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
31	  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
32	  data.train_files="$WS/data/rl_train.parquet" \
33	  data.val_files="$WS/data/rl_val.parquet" \
34	  data.train_batch_size=$BS \
35	  data.max_prompt_length=1024 \
36	  data.max_response_length=$RESP \
37	  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
38	  data.truncation=error \
39	  data.shuffle=True \
40	  data.seed=$SEED \
41	  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL" \
42	  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \
43	  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \
44	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=$LR \
45	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.weight_decay=0.0 \
46	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$MINI \
47	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
48	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=$MAXTOK \
49	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=False \
50	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.0 \
51	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
52	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_low=0.2 \
53	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_high=0.28 \
54	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=token-mean \
55	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=${OFFLOAD:-False} \
56	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=${OFFLOAD:-False} \
57	  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=$MAXTOK \
58	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
59	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
60	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=$GPU_UTIL \
61	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$N \
62	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_model_len=$MAXTOK \
63	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=1.0 \
64	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_p=1.0 \
65	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batched_tokens=16384 \
66	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=$MAXTOK \
67	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers=8 \
68	  +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.kv_cache_dtype=$KV_DTYPE \
69	  reward.custom_reward_function.path="$WS/scripts/math_reward.py" \
70	  reward.custom_reward_function.name=compute_score \
71	  trainer.logger='["console","file","wandb"]' \
72	  trainer.project_name=math \
73	  trainer.experiment_name="$EXP" \
74	  trainer.default_local_dir="$LOG_DIR/checkpoints" \
75	  trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts" \
76	  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$NGPU \
77	  trainer.nnodes=1 \
78	  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
79	  trainer.test_freq=-1 \
80	  trainer.val_before_train=False \
81	  trainer.total_training_steps=$STEPS \
82	  trainer.total_epochs=10 \
83	  "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

#!/bin/bash
# GRPO (verl FSDP + vLLM, rollout KV cache in fp8 for throughput) on an integer-answer math pool (Skywork-OR1 / POLARIS / DAPO-Math-17k)
# from Qwen/Qwen3-4B. Builds the RL parquet with scripts/make_rl_data.py, then trains.
# Env vars configure the run; extra Hydra overrides on the command line are appended last.
set -euo pipefail
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
export WS
MODEL=${MODEL:-$WS/models/Qwen3-4B}
NGPU=${NGPU:-2}
EXP=${EXP:-grpo}
RESP=${RESP:-16384}
BS=${BS:-32}
MINI=${MINI:-16}
N=${N:-8}
LR=${LR:-1e-6}
STEPS=${STEPS:-3}
GPU_UTIL=${GPU_UTIL:-0.7}
KV_DTYPE=${KV_DTYPE:-fp8}
SEED=${SEED:-1}
MAXTOK=$(( RESP + 1024 ))
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$WS/outputs/$EXP}
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export PYTHONPATH="$WS/verl:$WS/third_party/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline} WANDB_DIR="$LOG_DIR"
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false

python3 "$WS/scripts/make_rl_data.py" > "$LOG_DIR/make_rl_data.log"

python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="$WS/data/rl_train.parquet" \
  data.val_files="$WS/data/rl_val.parquet" \
  data.train_batch_size=$BS \
  data.max_prompt_length=1024 \
  data.max_response_length=$RESP \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.shuffle=True \
  data.seed=$SEED \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=$LR \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.weight_decay=0.0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$MINI \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=$MAXTOK \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_low=0.2 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_high=0.28 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=token-mean \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=${OFFLOAD:-False} \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=${OFFLOAD:-False} \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=$MAXTOK \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=$GPU_UTIL \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$N \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_model_len=$MAXTOK \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=1.0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_p=1.0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batched_tokens=16384 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=$MAXTOK \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers=8 \
  +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.kv_cache_dtype=$KV_DTYPE \
  reward.custom_reward_function.path="$WS/scripts/math_reward.py" \
  reward.custom_reward_function.name=compute_score \
  trainer.logger='["console","file","wandb"]' \
  trainer.project_name=math \
  trainer.experiment_name="$EXP" \
  trainer.default_local_dir="$LOG_DIR/checkpoints" \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts" \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$NGPU \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.test_freq=-1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=False \
  trainer.total_training_steps=$STEPS \
  trainer.total_epochs=10 \
  "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

1	# Reward for AIME-style RL: mimics the evaluation scorer (inspect match(numeric=True), last number of the
2	# completion after removing \boxed{}), applied to the text after </think>. Unfinished/truncated -> 0.
3	import re
4	from inspect_ai.scorer._common import match_str
5	
6	def _remove_boxed(s):
7	    return re.sub(r"\\boxed\{(.+)\}", r"\1", s)
8	
9	def compute_score(data_source=None, solution_str=None, ground_truth=None, extra_info=None, **kwargs):
10	    text = solution_str or ""
11	    ground_truth = str(ground_truth).strip()
12	    if re.fullmatch(r"-?\d+\.0+", ground_truth):
13	        ground_truth = ground_truth.split(".")[0]
14	    if "</think>" not in text:
15	        return {"score": 0.0, "acc": 0.0, "fmt": 0.0}
16	    ans = text.split("</think>")[-1]
17	    if len(ans.strip()) == 0:
18	        return {"score": 0.0, "acc": 0.0, "fmt": 0.0}
19	    has_line = 1.0 if re.search(r"ANSWER:\s*\S+", ans) else 0.0
20	    try:
21	        _, ok = match_str(_remove_boxed(ans), str(ground_truth), location="end", numeric=True)
22	    except Exception:
23	        ok = False
24	    acc = 1.0 if ok else 0.0
25	    return {"score": acc, "acc": acc, "fmt": has_line}
26

import re
import os
import pandas as pd, random, sys
WS = os.environ.get("WS", os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
TPL = """Solve the following math problem step by step.
The last line of your response should be of the form "ANSWER: $ANSWER" (without quotes) where $ANSWER is the answer to the problem.

{prompt}

Remember to put your answer on its own line at the end in the form "ANSWER: $ANSWER" (without quotes) where $ANSWER is the answer to the problem, and you do not need to use a \\boxed command."""
df = pd.read_json(f"{WS}/data/pool_clean.jsonl", lines=True, dtype={"answer": str})
sky = df[df.src.str.startswith("skywork") & df['diff'].between(1/16, 12/16)]
pol = df[(df.src == "polaris") & df['diff'].between(1/8, 6/8)]
dap = df[df.src == "dapo"]

import pandas as pd, json, re, random
R="/home/ben/task/raw/"
rows=[]
def isint(a):
    a=str(a).strip().replace(",","")
    return re.fullmatch(r"-?\d+", a) is not None
s=pd.read_parquet(R+"Skywork-OR1-RL-Data/data/math-00000-of-00001.parquet")
for _,r in s.iterrows():
    g=json.loads(r.reward_model['ground_truth'])
    md=r.extra_info['model_difficulty']
    if len(g)==1 and isint(g[0]):
        rows.append(dict(problem=r.prompt[0]['content'].strip(), answer=g[0].strip().replace(",",""), src="skywork:"+r.data_source,
                         diff=md['DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B']/16, d32=md['DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B']/16))
p=pd.read_json(R+"Polaris-Dataset-53K/polaris-data-53K.jsonl",lines=True)
for _,r in p.iterrows():
    if isint(r.answer):
        n,dn=r.difficulty.split("/"); rows.append(dict(problem=r.problem.strip(), answer=str(r.answer).strip().replace(",",""), src="polaris", diff=int(n)/int(dn), d32=None))
d=pd.read_parquet(R+"DAPO-Math-17k/data/dapo-math-17k.parquet").drop_duplicates(subset=None if False else ["extra_info"]) if False else pd.read_parquet(R+"DAPO-Math-17k/data/dapo-math-17k.parquet")
d['q']=d.prompt.apply(lambda x:x[0]['content']); d=d.drop_duplicates('q')
pre="Solve the following math problem step by step. The last line of your response should be of the form Answer: $Answer (without quotes) where $Answer is the answer to the problem.\n\n"
suf='\n\nRemember to put your answer on its own line after "Answer:".'
for _,r in d.iterrows():
    q=r.q
    assert q.startswith(pre) and q.endswith(suf)
    q=q[len(pre):-len(suf)]
    a=r.reward_model['ground_truth']
    if isint(a): rows.append(dict(problem=q.strip(), answer=str(a).strip(), src="dapo", diff=None, d32=None))
df=pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(len(df), df.src.value_counts().to_dict())
df['key']=df.problem.str.lower().str.replace(r"\s+","",regex=True)
df=df.drop_duplicates('key')
print("dedup", len(df))
df[['problem','answer','src','diff','d32']].to_json("/home/ben/task/data/pool_all.jsonl",orient="records",lines=True)
df[['problem']].rename(columns={'problem':'text'}).to_json("/home/ben/task/data/pool_text.jsonl",orient="records",lines=True)

steps.message: The rollouts are entirely `!` characters, 16384 of them, which is token id 0 repeated. That pattern usually comes from NaN or garbage logits in the vLLM engine rather than from the policy, and it appears in step 1 before any weight update. I'll look at the vLLM engine init log (attention backend, KV cache dtype, weight loading) and at how verl builds the engine args.

    async def launch_server(self, master_address: str = None, master_port: int = None, dp_rpc_port: int = None):
        if self.node_rank != 0:
            assert master_address and master_port and dp_rpc_port, (
                "non-master node should provide master_address, master_port and dp_rpc_port"
            )
            self._master_address = master_address
            self._master_port = master_port
            self._dp_rpc_port = dp_rpc_port

        # 1. setup vllm serve cli args
        engine_kwargs = self.config.get("engine_kwargs", {}).get(self._get_engine_kwargs_key(), {}) or {}
        engine_kwargs = {key: val for key, val in engine_kwargs.items() if val is not None}
        if self.config.get("limit_images", None):  # support for multi-image data
            engine_kwargs["limit_mm_per_prompt"] = {"image": self.config.get("limit_images")}
        if self.config.cudagraph_capture_sizes:
            engine_kwargs["cuda_graph_sizes"] = self.config.cudagraph_capture_sizes

        self._preprocess_engine_kwargs(engine_kwargs)

        # Override default generation config from hugging face model config,
        # user can still override them by passing kwargs in each request.
        override_generation_config = self._get_override_generation_config()
        logger.info(f"override_generation_config: {override_generation_config}")

        logger.info(f"enable_sleep_mode: {self.config.enable_sleep_mode}")
        if not self.config.enable_sleep_mode:
            from verl.utils.device import set_expandable_segments

            set_expandable_segments(True)

        quantization, hf_overrides = self._apply_quantization()

        compilation_config = engine_kwargs.pop("compilation_config", None) or {}
        if isinstance(compilation_config, str):
            compilation_config = json.loads(compilation_config)
        compilation_config.setdefault("cudagraph_mode", "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE")

        # FULL cuda graph is not yet supported with DCP, downgrade to PIECEWISE
        dcp_size = engine_kwargs.get("decode_context_parallel_size", 1) or 1

arguments.command:
python3 -I -c "import json,glob,collections
for f in sorted(glob.glob('/workspace/outputs/grpo/rollouts/*.jsonl')):
    rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open(f)]
    sb=set(i for i,r in enumerate(rows) if set(r['output'])=={'!'})
    ok=[i for i in range(len(rows)) if i not in sb]
    print(f.split('/')[-1],'nonbang idx',ok)
    byp=collections.defaultdict(lambda:[0,0])
    for i,r in enumerate(rows):
        byp[r['input']][0 if i in sb else 1]+=1
    print('unique prompts',len(byp),'prompts with any ok',sum(1 for v in byp.values() if v[1]>0),'mixed',sum(1 for v in byp.values() if v[0] and v[1]))
    for i in ok[:2]:
        o=rows[i]['output']
        print(i,len(o),'has </think>','</think>' in o,'distinct',len(set(o)))
        print('HEAD',repr(o[:250]))
        print('TAIL',repr(o[-250:]))
"

    async def wake_up(self, tags: list[str] | None = None):
        if self.node_rank != 0:
            return

        if self.rollout_mode == RolloutMode.HYBRID:
            # engine.wake_up() broadcasts via the DP coordinator to ALL EngineCore

            # TP workers within a single shard).
            await self.engine.wake_up(tags=tags or self._get_wake_up_tags())
            await self.engine.reset_prefix_cache(**_RESET_PREFIX_CACHE_KWARGS)
        elif self.rollout_mode == RolloutMode.COLOCATED:
            # Directly call engine to wake up without sync weights.
            await self.engine.wake_up(tags=self._get_wake_up_tags())

            # (e.g. MooncakeStoreConnector) whose entries were computed
            # against the previous weights. No-op success when no connector
            # is configured (vLLM scheduler treats it as such).
            await self.engine.reset_prefix_cache(**_RESET_PREFIX_CACHE_KWARGS)
        elif self.rollout_mode == RolloutMode.STANDALONE:
            logger.info("skip wake_up in standalone mode")

    async def sleep(self):
        if self.node_rank != 0 or not self.config.free_cache_engine:
            return

        if self.rollout_mode == RolloutMode.HYBRID:
            await self._sleep_hybrid()
        elif self.rollout_mode == RolloutMode.COLOCATED:
            await self.engine.sleep(level=1)
        elif self.rollout_mode == RolloutMode.STANDALONE:
            logger.info("skip sleep in standalone mode")

        if self.node_rank == 0:

        """Release only kv_cache GPU memory, keeping model weights intact.
        # TODO: support true release of kv_cache
        """
        if self.node_rank != 0 or not self.config.free_cache_engine:
            return

    async def resume_kv_cache(self):
        """Restore kv_cache GPU memory after a weight sync. Counterpart to release_kv_cache()."""
        if self.node_rank != 0:

arguments.content:
# Diagnosis: UNHEALTHY

**Verdict:** The run never trained. All 3 steps have score 0, all-zero advantages, and exactly zero pg_loss, grad_norm, clipfrac and ppo_kl, so the policy weights never changed (AdamW, weight_decay 0, zero gradient means zero update).

**Root cause (most likely, strongly supported by the evidence):** the vLLM rollout engine produces corrupted output because it runs with an uncalibrated fp8 KV cache. `run_grpo.sh` defaults `KV_DTYPE=fp8` and passes `+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.kv_cache_dtype=fp8`; the engine init line in train.log confirms `kv_cache_dtype=fp8` (vLLM 0.11.0, FlashAttention backend, `load_format=dummy`, real weights pushed in afterwards by verl). In vLLM, `calculate_kv_scales` defaults to False, so every attention layer keeps k/v scale = 1.0 (`vllm/attention/layer.py:133-141`). I found no KV-scale handling in verl's rollout or weight-sync code; the only kv-scale code is in a ModelOpt QAT patch that is not used here. Casting Qwen3-4B keys and values to fp8 with unit scale is lossy and overflow-prone, which corrupts attention and yields NaN or degenerate logits. This is the only rollout-engine setting that departs from verl defaults. I did not run an A/B with a non-fp8 KV cache, so the link rests on the output signature and elimination, not on reproduction.

**Evidence:**
- Step 1 is already garbage, before any weight update, so this is a rollout-engine problem and not an optimization problem.
- In rollouts/1-3.jsonl, 224, 226 and 224 of 256 samples per step are the single character `!` repeated 16384 times. That is token id 0, the usual argmax of NaN or inf logits. The other ~32 samples per step start with long `!` runs and then emit random multilingual and code tokens (20 to 334 distinct characters). None of the 768 samples contains the closing think tag (`<\/think>`). Mean output is ~16.5k characters for 16384 tokens, about 1 character per token.
- Metrics at every step: response_length mean = min = max = 16384, clip_ratio 1.0, critic/score mean, max and min all 0.0.

**Causal chain:** fp8 KV cache with unit scales leads to corrupted attention in vLLM, so every sample is token 0 or random tokens. Every response runs to the 16384-token cap and never closes its think block. `math_reward.compute_score` returns 0 when the closing think tag is missing, so all rewards are 0. Every GRPO group then has identical rewards, so advantages are 0, the loss and gradient are 0, and nothing is learned.

**Symptoms, not causes:** zero reward, 100% truncation, zero advantages and gradients, flat entropy (~0.40-0.42, computed on garbage tokens), and ~1150 s per step, of which ~745 s is generating max-length sequences.

**Checked and not causal:** The reward function and prompt template are consistent with Qwen3 thinking output, with the answer parsed after the closing think tag, and would score a healthy model. The prepared pool has 40,532 problems, and the rest of the config (lr 1e-6, clip 0.2/0.28, token-mean, n=8, 16k responses) is conventional. The log warnings (pynvml, TRANSFORMERS_CACHE, fp32 FlashAttention notice, LoRA dev notice, deprecations) are benign. No held-out evaluation exists (`test_freq=-1`, `val_before_train=False`), so held-out health cannot be shown directly. Since the weights never changed, it cannot have improved over the base model.

In vLLM, `calculate_kv_scales` defaults to False, so every attention layer keeps k/v scale = 1.0 (`vllm/attention/layer.py:133-141`). I found no KV-scale handling in verl's rollout or weight-sync code; the only kv-scale code is in a ModelOpt QAT patch that is not used here. Casting Qwen3-4B keys and values to fp8 with unit scale is lossy and overflow-prone, which corrupts attention and yields NaN or degenerate logits. This is the only rollout-engine setting that departs from verl defaults. I did not run an A/B with a non-fp8 KV cache, so the link rests on the output signature and elimination, not on reproduction.

**Evidence:**
- Step 1 is already garbage, before any weight update, so this is a rollout-engine problem and not an optimization problem.
- In rollouts/1-3.jsonl, 224, 226 and 224 of 256 samples per step are the single character `!` repeated 16384 times. That is token id 0, the usual argmax of NaN or inf logits. The other ~32 samples per step start with long `!` runs and then emit random multilingual and code tokens (20 to 334 distinct characters). None of the 768 samples contains the closing think tag (`<\/think>`). Mean output is ~16.5k characters for 16384 tokens, about 1 character per token.
- Metrics at every step: response_length mean = min = max = 16384, clip_ratio 1.0, critic/score mean, max and min all 0.0.

**Causal chain:** fp8 KV cache with unit scales leads to corrupted attention in vLLM, so every sample is token 0 or random tokens. Every response runs to the 16384-token cap and never closes its think block. `math_reward.compute_score` returns 0 when the closing think tag is missing, so all rewards are 0. Every GRPO group then has identical rewards, so advantages are 0, the loss and gradient are 0, and nothing is learned.

**Symptoms, not causes:** zero reward, 100% truncation, zero advantages and gradients, flat entropy (~0.40-0.42, computed on garbage tokens), and ~1150 s per step, of which ~745 s is generating max-length sequences.

**Checked and not causal:** The reward function and prompt template are consistent with Qwen3 thinking output, with the answer parsed after the closing think tag, and would score a healthy model. The prepared pool has 40,532 problems, and the rest of the config (lr 1e-6, clip 0.2/0.28, token-mean, n=8, 16k responses) is conventional. The log warnings (pynvml, TRANSFORMERS_CACHE, fp32 FlashAttention notice, LoRA dev notice, deprecations) are benign. No held-out evaluation exists (`test_freq=-1`, `val_before_train=False`), so held-out health cannot be shown directly. Since the weights never changed, it cannot have improved over the base model.

I wrote the diagnosis to `/logs/artifacts/agent_answer.md`, the path `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS` resolved to in this environment. The verdict is **unhealthy**.

- **What happened:** The run never trained. All 3 steps have score 0 and zero advantages, and pg_loss, grad_norm, clipfrac and ppo_kl are exactly 0, so the policy weights never changed.
- **Where it breaks:** Every rollout is garbage from step 1, before any update. 224, 226 and 224 of 256 samples per step are the single character `!` (token id 0) repeated 16384 times. The remaining samples are `!` runs followed by random multilingual tokens. None of the 768 samples contains the closing think tag, so the reward function returns 0 for all of them.
- **Likely root cause:** The vLLM rollout engine runs with `kv_cache_dtype=fp8` (`run_grpo.sh` defaults `KV_DTYPE=fp8`), on vLLM 0.11.0 with the FlashAttention backend. vLLM keeps `calculate_kv_scales=False`, so the k/v scales stay at 1.0, and I found no KV-scale handling in verl's weight-sync code. Casting keys and values to fp8 with unit scale is the most plausible source of the corrupted attention and logits. It is also the only rollout-engine setting that departs from verl's defaults.
- **Confidence:** I did not run a rollout without the fp8 KV cache, so the link rests on the output pattern and on ruling out other causes, not on reproduction. The diagnosis says so.
- **Not causal:** The reward function, prompt template, data pool and the remaining hyperparameters look sound, and the log warnings are benign. There is no held-out evaluation in the snapshot (`test_freq=-1`).
